title: Prefix cache observed-vs-simulated hit-rate/latency mapper and regression sentinel
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible harness that maps real observed prefix-cache workloads to simulated traffic profiles and produces a compact fingerprint per run. The harness must sweep token/sec, working set size, and memory pressure to produce hit-rate vs p95 latency curves and export deterministic artifacts consumed by CI and the monitoring stack.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay representative traffic traces with adjustable token/sec and concurrency
Output includes: tokens_per_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, prefix_cache_hit_rate, memory_used_bytes, kv_eviction_rate
Run artifacts include a stable fingerprint and a JSON summary that the regression detector can diff
Integration with CI: failing differential beyond thresholds triggers an automated GitHub PR comment and a Canary alert in Datadog
Dashboard tile in Console showing run-to-run comparison and heatmap of hit-rate vs p95
steps: Collect 3 production traces (chat, completions, embeddings) and anonymize prefix keys — link to Drive: https://drive.company/rd/pfx-traces
Implement traffic synthesizer: variable token/sec generator, prefix selector based on Zipfian/recency mix
Add memory throbber to induce controlled GC/eviction cycles to emulate memory pressure
Record profiler hooks and KV runtime counters (cache hits/misses, evictions, slab usage)
Produce deterministic fingerprint: combine trace hash + config params + sampled histogram seeds
Wire output to regression detector job that diffs new fingerprint against baseline and computes percentage regressions on p95 and tokens/sec
results_summary: Initial runs on a 4-GPU dev cluster show clear knee points: hit-rate > 85% yields <20ms p95 for short contexts but degrades quickly above 75% working set churn. Memory-induced eviction spikes correlate with 2x p95 regressions. We captured stable fingerprints for the three baseline traces and created a failing-case sample to exercise the detector.
